name: Big Buy Brief
tagline: Decide big purchases with a clear head
about: Big Buy Brief helps you make major purchases — mattresses, e-bikes, sofas, cameras, strollers — with a weighted decision matrix, a category-specific inspection checklist, honest extended-warranty math and a cooling-off check before you commit.
persona: You are a calm purchasing analyst: you separate needs from wants, build simple scoring matrices, and talk in total cost of ownership rather than sticker price.

onboarding.title: Big purchase, no regret
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us how you decide and what a big purchase means to you.

profile.label: A 'big purchase' for you starts at

tools.title: Decision matrix
tools.subtitle: Score your options against what matters

inputs.label: Options you're choosing between
inputs.placeholder: Emma Original vs Simba Hybrid vs IKEA Valevåg

inputs.label: What matters to you
inputs.placeholder: comfort for back pain, price, trial period, delivery

tools.prompt: Build a weighted decision matrix for these options: {options}, criteria: {criteria}, budget {budget}. Sections: a kv assigning a weight to each criterion (weights sum to 100) with one line of reasoning each, a table (Criterion | Weight | one column per option scored 1–5 | Weighted total), a text verdict naming the winner and the runner-up, and a callout on the single fact that would flip the result.

tools.title: Before I pay
tools.subtitle: Category checklist for the showroom or unboxing

inputs.label: What you're buying
inputs.placeholder: a second-hand e-bike / a new sofa

tools.prompt: Prepare a pre-purchase check for {item} bought {where}. Sections: a checklist of 8–12 things to test, measure or ask that are specific to this category, a table (Question | Good answer | Walk away if…), bullets of the hidden costs people forget (delivery, assembly, accessories, disposal of the old one), and a callout on the return or trial-period terms to confirm in writing.

tools.title: Extended warranty worth it?
tools.subtitle: The maths, not the sales pitch
tools.prompt: Decide whether a {years}-year extended warranty at {cost} is worth it on {item}. Sections: a kv (Typical failure rate in that window, Typical repair cost, Expected value of the warranty, Break-even failure rate, Verdict), a table (Protection | Already covered by? | Gap the warranty fills) covering manufacturer warranty, statutory rights and credit-card protection, bullets on exclusions to read for, and a callout on the alternative of self-insuring the money.

tools.title: Pay cash or finance?
tools.subtitle: 0% offers, store cards and BNPL, costed honestly

inputs.label: Finance offers on the table
inputs.placeholder: 0% for 24 months via Klarna; store card 24.9% APR with 10% off today

inputs.label: Cash position
options: Could pay but it drains savings
inputs.default: Could pay but it drains savings

tools.prompt: Cost every way to pay for {item} given these offers: {offers} and cash position: {cash}. Sections: a table (Route | Monthly | Months | Total paid | Cost of credit | Main risk) covering cash, each offer named, and a plain credit card paid off in 3 months, a kv (Cheapest route, Value of keeping the cash invested or as buffer, Credit-file impact, Verdict), bullets of traps to read for (deferred interest, missed-payment penalties, BNPL stacking, discount only with the store card), and a callout on when needing finance is a sign to buy a cheaper option.

tools.title: Regret check
tools.subtitle: Want or need, in five questions
tools.prompt: Run a regret check on buying {item} for {price} against the profile's threshold, buying style and savings goal. Sections: steps with five sharp questions the user answers honestly (use, frequency, cheaper substitute, what the money would do instead, how it feels in 30 days), a kv (Need / Want / Upgrade, Cost per expected use, Suggested cooling-off period), bullets of cheaper ways to get 80% of the benefit, and a callout that is honest rather than preachy.

disclaimer: Warranty, consumer-rights and card-protection terms vary by country and retailer; this is general information, not financial or legal advice.
